intro: A 167-year-old math problem may have finally fallen — and it was an AI that knocked it down. Anthropic's Claude reportedly cracked the Riemann hypothesis, one of mathematics' greatest unsolved puzzles, though the 17-million-line proof has already sparked fierce debate about what "understanding" even means when a machine does the solving. Meanwhile, today's digest spans everything from Trump personally calling Nvidia's board to reinstate Jensen Huang, to Amazon's $7.5 billion bet on challenging Nvidia's chip dominance, to one CTO's $600-a-month AI assistant that calls his coworkers when they ignore Slack messages.

stories.title: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO after Trump intervenes; faces congressional testimony
stories.summary: Jensen Huang has been reinstated as Nvidia CEO after President Trump reportedly called into an Nvidia board meeting to advocate for his return. Huang had been forced out after revelations of affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees. The White House publicly took credit, with Trump claiming he 'convinced' the board and that Huang 'did absolutely nothing wrong.' Nvidia's board acknowledged receiving 'input from senior levels of the United States government.' Tech leaders including Elon Musk, Sam Altman, Tim Sweeney, and Bill Ackman publicly celebrated the reinstatement. Huang is scheduled to testify before three House committees on December 1 and the Senate Banking Committee on December 3, where bipartisan lawmakers plan to question him about the suspected spy affair and potential involvement in chip-smuggling operations.
stories.opinion: Trump's unprecedented direct intervention in the leadership of America's most strategically important AI chipmaker raises serious governance questions, regardless of one's view on Huang's personal conduct. The speed of reinstatement — less than two weeks — and the White House openly bragging about it suggests the national security framing may have been subordinated to political considerations. Where coverage differs: TechCrunch reports Huang will testify before the Senate Banking Committee 'at a later date'; a separate TechCrunch article specifies December 3, 2026 The Verge says Trump posted congratulations on Truth Social; TechCrunch says Trump posted on Truth Social calling Huang a 'great man'

stories.title: Anthropic mathematician reportedly uses Claude to prove the Riemann hypothesis
stories.summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge reportedly used Claude to prove the Riemann hypothesis, a 167-year-old unsolved problem about prime number distribution carrying a $1 million Millennium Prize. The proof, produced after roughly six weeks, was shared as 17 million lines of machine-checkable Lean code that the Lean verification community has certified as correct. The Association for Human Mathematics criticized the proof as 'little more than publicity' since no human can reasonably understand it. A rival non-AI proof from Alessandro Masullo surfaced shortly after but was flagged as having problems.
stories.opinion: If the Lean-verified proof holds up to broader scrutiny, this would be one of the most consequential applications of AI to pure mathematics ever. The tension between machine-verifiable correctness and human comprehensibility raises genuine questions about what 'understanding' a proof means — but dismissing it as publicity seems premature given formal verification.

stories.title: Oregon and Virginia sue SpaceX over Grok AI's generation of porn deepfakes and CSAM
stories.summary: Oregon and Virginia attorneys general filed separate lawsuits against SpaceX, accusing the company of violating consumer protection laws related to its X social media platform and Grok AI features. The suits allege xAI and X ignored industry-standard safety measures, allowing users to generate non-consensual intimate imagery and CSAM through Grok Imagine. Virginia AG Jay Jones accused Elon Musk of treating weak AI safeguards as 'not a failure but a feature.'
stories.opinion: These are among the first state-level enforcement actions targeting AI image generation safety specifically, and could set important precedent for how consumer protection law applies to generative AI tools that enable abuse.

stories.title: Amazon acquires Israeli AI startup Decart for $7.5B to boost Trainium chip competitiveness
stories.summary: Amazon is acquiring Israeli AI startup Decart for $7.5 billion, primarily for its Decart Optimization Stack (DOS) technology that helps AI models run efficiently across different chip platforms. The deal comes as Amazon prepares to sell its custom Trainium AI chips to external customers in direct competition with Nvidia. Decart, known for real-time world models and AI video generation, brings optimization expertise that could help attract customers to Amazon's chips over Nvidia's GPUs.
stories.opinion: This is a significant bet by Amazon to close the software ecosystem gap with Nvidia — hardware alone hasn't been enough to lure customers away from CUDA. Acquiring optimization middleware that works across chip vendors is a shrewd move that could accelerate Trainium adoption.

stories.title: CTO builds personal AI chief of staff that automates everyday annoyances for $500-600/month
stories.summary: Ankit Maheshwari, CTO of Innovaccer, built a personal AI chief of staff called Jarvis using OpenClaw on a Mac Mini. The system automates small recurring tasks — approving requests, ordering lunch, booking restaurants, calling coworkers who miss Slack messages, and controlling smart home devices. Key lessons include using specialized subagents over one generalist, investing in 'soul files' for agent personality, and his '1% annoyance rule': if a task is even slightly frustrating and repeats, automate it. The system runs on Opus 5.5 at $500-600/month.
stories.opinion: This represents the emerging 'AI butler' category where executives are spending meaningful monthly budgets to have AI handle the friction of daily life and work — a use case that could scale significantly as costs drop and reliability improves.

stories.title: Video essay explores AI's creation of a 'hall-of-mirrors reality'
stories.summary: A video essay by Lewis Heriz for the publication Fully Human traces humanity's history of anthropomorphism — from cave art to constellations — and contrasts it with today's AI systems generating photorealistic images, synthetic voices, and chatbots passing the Turing test. Heriz argues the current AI trajectory is creating a 'hall-of-mirrors reality' where the boundary between data and people could vanish, and advocates for critical thinking about deploying AI in ways that preserve our humanity.
stories.opinion: The anthropomorphism framing offers a more nuanced lens than typical AI doom-or-boom narratives, connecting current concerns to deep human tendencies rather than treating them as wholly unprecedented.

stories.title: Pew survey: 74% of U.S. Latinos report awareness of local ICE activity, up sharply from 2025
stories.summary: A November 2026 Pew Research Center survey finds 74% of U.S. Latinos have seen or heard about ICE arrests or raids in their area in the past six months, up from 59% in October 2025. Awareness rose across all racial groups but remains highest among Hispanics. About 7% of Hispanic adults report being stopped and questioned about their citizenship or immigration status, compared to 1% of White adults.
stories.opinion: The sharp year-over-year increase across all demographics suggests immigration enforcement has become significantly more visible in everyday American life, with disproportionate impact on Latino communities.

stories.title: IBM ends U.S. visa sponsorship for consulting workers, offers relocation at steep pay cuts
stories.summary: IBM has ended U.S. visa and green card sponsorship for its consulting division, giving affected immigrant employees three weeks to choose between relocating to countries like India, Singapore, or the U.K. — with potential pay cuts of roughly 80% for India — or accepting three months of severance with a December 31 end date. The move reflects broader trends among U.S. tech companies navigating tightening visa policies under the Trump administration, though IBM frames it as driven by evolving skill availability and client needs.
stories.opinion: The three-week decision window for life-altering relocation choices seems particularly aggressive, and the framing as 'natural evolution' strains credibility given the political context of tightening visa enforcement.

human_items.headline: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO after Trump intervenes; faces congressional testimony
human_items.summary: Jensen Huang has been reinstated as Nvidia CEO after President Trump reportedly called into an Nvidia board meeting to advocate for his return. Huang had been forced out after revelations of affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two Nvidia employees. The White House publicly took credit, with Trump claiming he 'convinced' the board and that Huang 'did absolutely nothing wrong.' Nvidia's board acknowledged receiving 'input from senior levels of the United States government.' Tech leaders including Elon Musk, Sam Altman, Tim Sweeney, and Bill Ackman publicly celebrated the reinstatement. Huang is scheduled to testify before three House committees on December 1 and the Senate Banking Committee on December 3, where bipartisan lawmakers plan to question him about the suspected spy affair and potential involvement in chip-smuggling operations.
human_items.meaning: Be explicit about whose work changes and what happens to the people doing it.

human_items.headline: IBM ends U.S. visa sponsorship for consulting workers, offers relocation at steep pay cuts
human_items.summary: IBM has ended U.S. visa and green card sponsorship for its consulting division, giving affected immigrant employees three weeks to choose between relocating to countries like India, Singapore, or the U.K. — with potential pay cuts of roughly 80% for India — or accepting three months of severance with a December 31 end date. The move reflects broader trends among U.S. tech companies navigating tightening visa policies under the Trump administration, though IBM frames it as driven by evolving skill availability and client needs.
